title: Hacker gets 8 years for stealing $3.3 million from taxpayers
description: A Nigerian national was sentenced to eight years in prison for spearphishing attacks targeting US tax preparation businesses from 2019 to 2021. The attacks resulted in the theft of personal and tax information from at least 800 customers, leading to fraudulent tax refunds and loan applications totaling over $3.3 million. The defendant also participated in a fake investment scheme that defrauded victims of more than $7 million. He was extradited from France and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit computer intrusions and wire fraud. The court ordered restitution and forfeiture totaling nearly $15 million.
aiSummary: Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu, a Nigerian national, was involved in spearphishing campaigns targeting US tax preparation firms across multiple states between 2019 and 2021. These attacks enabled unauthorized access to victim computers, resulting in the theft of personally identifiable information and tax data of at least 800 customers. Using this stolen data, Amachukwu and co-conspirators filed fraudulent tax refund claims amounting to $8.4 million, of which approximately $2.5 million was obtained, and secured $819,000 through fraudulent loan applications with the SBA's Economic Injury Disaster Loan program. Additionally, Amachukwu engaged in a fraudulent investment scheme involving fake standby letters of credit, defrauding victims of over $7 million. After extradition from France, he pleaded guilty to conspiracy charges and was sentenced to eight years imprisonment, one year supervised release, and ordered to pay $3.6 million restitution and forfeit nearly $11 million.
aiImpact: The spearphishing attacks led to significant financial losses exceeding $3.3 million through fraudulent tax refunds and loan applications. The fraudulent investment scheme caused additional losses of over $7 million. The attacks compromised sensitive personal and tax information of at least 800 individuals, causing harm to victims and public trust in tax preparation services. The defendant's conviction and sentencing demonstrate law enforcement's ability to hold cybercriminals accountable.
